text: In this way. <break time="0.8s" /> Dupin said. <break time="0.8s" /> The boy could match his own mind. <break time="0.8s" /> With his opponents mind. <break time="0.8s" /> And guess what the other would do. <break time="0.8s" /> The Prefect, however. <break time="0.8s" /> Never considered the mind. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the man he was hunting. <break time="0.8s" /> Searching only the places. <break time="0.8s" /> Where he himself would have hidden it. <break time="0.8s" /> So fixed was he. <break time="0.8s" /> On his own ideas of cleverness. <break time="0.8s" /> That he never imagined. <break time="0.8s" /> A hiding place outside the usual ones. <break time="0.8s" /> The Minister on the other hand. <break time="0.8s" /> Was both a poet and a mathematician. <break time="0.8s" /> Which meant. <break time="0.8s" /> That he could reason as well as imagine. <break time="0.8s" /> Knowing that the police would search his house. <break time="0.8s" /> He had stayed away at night on purpose. <break time="0.8s" /> So that they could search it freely. <break time="0.8s" /> He wanted them to believe. <break time="0.8s" /> That the letter was not in the house. <break time="0.8s" /> So he would naturally choose. <break time="0.8s" /> A simple hiding place. <break time="0.8s" /> Dupin then mentioned a puzzle game. <break time="0.8s" /> In which one player names a word on a map. <break time="0.8s" /> And the other must find it. <break time="0.8s" /> Beginners choose names. <break time="0.8s" /> In the smallest letters. <break time="0.8s" /> But experts choose words in large letters. <break time="0.8s" /> That stretch across the whole map. <break time="0.8s" /> Such words. <break time="0.8s" /> Being too plain. <break time="0.8s" /> Escape the eye. <break time="0.8s" /> And Dupin became sure. <break time="0.8s" /> That the Minister had hidden the letter. <break time="0.8s" /> By not hiding it at all.
